question.problem:
Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that a student gets $14$ correct answers on a true/false quiz with $25$ questions if the student answers all questions at random. Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6554\,$ | $\,0.6591\,$ | $\,0.6628\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7257\,$ | $\,0.7291\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7881\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=25$ and $p=0.5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =25\cdot 0.5 \\  & =12.5 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =25\cdot (1-0.5) \\  & =12.5 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(25)(0.5)=12.5
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(25)(0.5)(1-0.5)=6.25.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(12.5,6.25).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=14).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=14)≈P(13.5\le Y\le 14.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(13.5\le Y\le 14.5) & =P(\frac{13.5-12.5}{\sqrt{6.25}}\le Z\le \frac{14.5-12.5}{\sqrt{6.25}}) \\  & ≈P(0.40\le Z\le 0.80) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.80)-P(Z<0.40) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.80)-P(Z\le 0.40) \\  & =Φ(0.80)-Φ(0.40) \\  & =0.7881-0.6554 \\  & =0.1327\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=14)≈0.133.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.1327.$
